Czech Republic.text: Budweis was brewing "Budweiser" long before Anheuser-Busch; in North America the Czech one is sold as Czechvar.
Czech Republic.evidence: The city was for centuries also known by its German name, Budweis. Brewing is recorded here since the 13th century, and the beer produced was commonly referred to as Budweiser Bier (pivo z Českých Budějovic). The modern Budějovický měšťanský pivovar was founded in 1795 as the Bürgerliches Brauhaus Budweis and is the oldest brewery in the world to use the term "budweiser" when referring to its beer. ... In 1876, the US brewer Anheuser-Busch began making a beer that it also called Budweiser. ... Budvar is sold in the United States and Canada under the label Czechvar

Austria.text: Freistadt's brewery is owned and run by the people who own a house inside the old town walls.
Austria.evidence: Freistadt in Upper Austria is also home to Freistädter Bier, a brewery owned and operated by those who own a house within the city walls.

Romania.text: Romanian law treats beer and wine as foodstuffs, so they escape the usual tariffs and restrictions on alcohol.
Romania.evidence: Romanian law considers beer and wine to be foodstuffs and therefore they are not subject to the usual tariffs and restrictions imposed upon alcoholic beverages.

Germany.text: The village of Aufseß, near Bamberg, has four breweries for 1,352 people, the world's highest density.
Germany.evidence: The highest density of breweries in the world is found in Aufseß near the city of Bamberg, in the Franconia region of Bavaria, with four breweries and only 1,352 citizens.

Poland.text: Its historic smoked wheat beer, Grodziskie, was nicknamed "Polish Champagne" and once exported to 37 countries.
Poland.evidence: Grodziskie ... is a historical beer style from Poland made from oak-smoked wheat malt ... It was nicknamed "Polish Champagne" because of its high carbonation levels ... At the peak of its fame, it was exported to 37 countries

Namibia.text: Namibia Breweries brews all its beers to the Reinheitsgebot, Germany's beer purity law of 1516.
Namibia.evidence: NBL brew all of their beers according to the Reinheitsgebot (German purity law) from 1516.

Ireland.text: Ireland's 18th-century parliament used taxes to favour brewing over distilling, deeming beer less harmful than whiskey.
Ireland.evidence: In the 18th century, the Irish Parliament used taxation to encourage brewing at the expense of distilling, reasoning that beer was less harmful than whiskey.

Spain.text: Its San Miguel beer began as a Philippine brand, brought over by a 1953 "Manila Agreement".
Spain.evidence: The shareholders of La Segarra signed the "Manila Agreement" in 1953 with the Chairman of the San Miguel Corporation of the Philippines, Andrés Soriano. The agreement granted a branding rights for San Miguel Spain.

Croatia.text: Its favourite beer, Ožujsko, goes down at a rate of 10 bottles every second.
Croatia.evidence: Ožujsko is the most popular beer in Croatia, with 10 bottles being consumed every second.

Latvia.text: Before the Baltic Crusades brought in Western brewing, Latvians flavoured their beer with herbs instead of hops.
Latvia.evidence: Ancient Latvians brewed beer (alus), mead (miestiņš) and honey beer (medalus) before the 13th century ... After the Baltic Crusades, the local beer brewing was influenced by the incoming Western European techniques. For example, prior to that, many herbs were used, but they were replaced by hops as a preservative and flavoring agent.
